explanation: `incrementToRange` is a linear map the library defines itself. It sends an element of the kernel submodule `F.increment i`, whose elements lie in a supported range, to the same underlying vector, now viewed in `LinearMap.range q`. The map is built by hand as `⟨x.1.1, x.1.2.1⟩`; it is not Mathlib's `Submodule.inclusion`. So its injectivity comes down to the library's own definition, and the proof only peels off subtypes with `Subtype.ext` twice. Only generic structural principles are involved, which don't count under the rules. No Mathlib lemma carries this content, so I found no duplicate. I read the definition and its proof in `TransfiniteRangeBasis.lean` and searched the library for every use of `incrementToRange`.
